solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crass act? No! Strangely seen as beyond criticism

indicators.note: letters behaving strangely are out of their usual order, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: all ten letters of the three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a crude act is being treated as untouchable.
explanation.walkthrough: The punctuation dresses the fodder up as an outburst; the letters of 'Crass act no' rearrange to SACROSANCT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacrosanct is regarded as too sacred or important to be attacked or questioned.

clue.text: Tendon — there's something wrong we turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up makes it read from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong act
taken as written, then read backwards

explanation.surface: A sporting injury: the tendon has gone wrong and we found out.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN, then WE flipped to EW, gives SINEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is the everyday word for a tendon, the tough cord joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Crack a word code for oil source

indicators.note: to crack a code is to work it out, implying the letters must be broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A spy is told to break a coded message to learn where the oil comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' and 'code' make a convincing espionage picture, but 'a word code' is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedarwood is distilled to produce an aromatic essential oil, so the wood is a source of oil.

clue.text: Oscar, rugby player, outstanding

blocks.note: Oscar is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for O
a wing is a rugby position, a fast player on the flank

explanation.surface: Praise for a rugby player named Oscar who had an outstanding game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the player, but it means still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still owing, not yet paid off.

clue.text: Help from Shanghai donation in part

indicators.note: the answer is only a part of the words that follow, sitting inside them

blocks.note: the last two letters of the first word plus the first of the second

explanation.surface: Assistance arriving partly through a donation from Shanghai.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the join: ShanghAI Donation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid and help are direct synonyms, both meaning assistance given to someone.

clue.text: Hard task including a learner in hymn tune

indicators.note: one thing including others holds them inside its own letters

blocks.note: a chore is a tedious, hard task
taken as written
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Learning a hymn tune is hard work for a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: A and L go inside CHORE, between its R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a stately hymn melody of the Lutheran kind, harmonised for congregational singing.

clue.text: Old bouncer resolved description of high quality cook

indicators.note: resolved suggests something broken down and worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters of both words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A retired nightclub bouncer has decided to become a top chef.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' reads as 'determined', but it is the signal to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cordon bleu, from the French blue ribbon, is applied to cooking or cooks of the highest class.

clue.text: Acknowledged love — married around November

indicators.note: the married word goes around the letter for November, holding it inside

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
to wed is to marry
November is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for N

explanation.surface: A couple admit their love and marry in late autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: O, then WED wrapped around N.
explanation.definitionFit: To have owned a fault is to have admitted or confessed it, an older sense of own.

clue.text: Popular party tourist regularly within building

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means every other one, at a fixed interval

blocks.note: something in is fashionable
a do is a party or social event
second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A well-attended tourist party is held inside a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoors means inside a building rather than out in the open.

clue.text: "Very little in street" — hear Tom's first girlfriend

indicators.note: one word placed in another sits inside its letters
first asks for the opening letter of the name only

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street
wee is Scottish for very small
taken as written
the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Tom's girlfriend is overheard being called a tiny thing in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Very little in street' look like overheard speech, but it is a container instruction; 'wee' is Scots for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a person one is in love with, so a girlfriend or boyfriend.

clue.text: Straightforward Irish county? Correct

blocks.note: County Down is in Northern Ireland
right means correct

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking whether a named Irish county is the right answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means plain and frank, so a straightforward person speaks without evasion.

clue.text: Worker south of fortified area is incisive

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word placed south of another is written below it, so it comes after

blocks.note: a trench is a dug-in defensive position
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A soldier digging in below a fortified position cuts through the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of' in a down clue puts ANT below TRENCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Trenchant comment is sharp and cutting, which is what incisive means.

clue.text: Some era — generally a long period

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are used, a run lying inside them

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word and first two of the second

explanation.surface: A historian's remark that an era is generally a long stretch of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the join: erA GEnerally. 'Some era' looks like a phrase; 'Some' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An age is a long stretch of time, as in the Bronze Age or 'I waited for ages'.

clue.text: Idea that's unacceptable about island

indicators.note: the unacceptable phrase is wrapped about the island letter, enclosing it

blocks.note: 'not on' is a British phrase for unacceptable
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a proposal concerning an island as out of the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not on' is everyday British speech for 'that's unacceptable', and the phrase splits around the island letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a concept or belief, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Letter from Greece put in container for Asian

indicators.note: something put in a container ends up inside it

blocks.note: a tin is a metal container
beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A letter posted from Greece is placed in a parcel bound for Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter from Greece' looks like post, but it means a letter of the Greek alphabet, inserted after the second letter of the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tibetan is a native of Tibet, a region of Asia, so is one kind of Asian.

clue.text: Fitting move downwards when son moves out

indicators.note: a son moving out leaves the household, so that letter leaves the word

blocks.note: a descent is a movement downwards
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A family suggests it is right for the son to move out and downsize.
explanation.walkthrough: DESCENT minus S leaves DECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent behaviour is proper or appropriate, which is what fitting means as an adjective.

clue.text: Left Old Boy, shy

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
OB is the abbreviation for Old Boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil who has departed is described as timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb for throwing.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to fling or toss something, and to lob is to throw it in a high arc.

clue.text: Clued "bide" in new way that can be worked out?

indicators.note: arranging the letters in a new way means placing them in a different order

blocks.note: the nine letters of both words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A setter boasts of a fresh way of cluing the word 'bide' that solvers can crack.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deducible can be inferred by reasoning, which is to say figured out.

clue.text: Clever contrivance of Venetian magistrate restricting Duke

indicators.note: restricting something means hemming it in, so the magistrate's title encloses the duke's letter

blocks.note: the Doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A Venetian official cunningly curbs the power of a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: Doges ruled Venice for about a thousand years until 1797; the duke's letter lands in the middle of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a crafty trick or scheme, so a clever contrivance fits as a noun.

clue.text: Club, extremely tacky, eccentric

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: a bat is a club used in cricket or baseball
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tasteless, eccentric nightclub is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a nightclub, but it is the bat; 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: Batty is informal for slightly mad, odd or crazy, so a synonym of eccentric.

clue.text: With no Test experience?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cricketer or rugby player who has never played an international Test match
setter's reading: never having been tested or tried out at all, so inexperienced

explanation.walkthrough: The capital T in Test points to international sport, but the answer is the general word for something not yet put to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Untried means not yet tested or proven by experience, which covers an uncapped player too.

clue.text: African language? Is bang on initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A guess that a named African language is exactly right.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibo, also spelt Igbo, is a major language of south-eastern Nigeria.

clue.text: Modify church table, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard said, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: the altar is the communion table in a church

explanation.surface: An instruction to rearrange the communion table in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: ALTAR and ALTER are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to change it, so it is a direct synonym of modify.

clue.text: Rudely having feature of shoe at edges, not lovely

indicators.note: at edges asks for only the outermost letters of each of the following words

blocks.note: the insole is the inner sole of a shoe
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a shoe that is far from attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: INSOLE + NT + LY. 'Not lovely' looks like a verdict on the shoe; 'at edges' applies to both words.
explanation.definitionFit: To act insolently is to behave with disrespectful rudeness, so the adverbs are synonyms.
